title: Flying with a gun
summary: Tell the airline in advance, pack the gun unloaded in a lockable hard case, and keep cartridges within the IATA and airline limits.

body.html: Start with the airline, even before you buy the ticket. Not all airlines carry sporting guns, and some carry them only on certain flights. Most ask for notice in advance, often at least a day or two. There may be a fee. Read the airline's rules on its website and get confirmation in writing.

The gun travels only in checked baggage, not in the cabin. It must be unloaded, usually taken down (barrels off the stock), and packed in a lockable hard case. A soft gun slip is usually not accepted for a flight. Rules on locks and on who keeps the keys differ, so check them.

Arrive at the airport earlier than usual. At check-in, say that you are carrying a sporting gun. Staff often open the case to check it, give you a separate paper for it, and send the case to the oversized-baggage counter instead of the usual belt. After landing, you may have to collect the gun at a separate desk, sometimes with a police officer present.

Cartridges count as ‘dangerous goods’ (things that are risky to carry on a plane), so they travel under their own rules. The IATA rules (IATA is the airlines' international association) allow sporting cartridges in checked baggage only, with the airline's approval, up to 5 kg per person including packaging, for your own use. ‘Gross’ means that the weight of the boxes counts too. Pack them firmly, usually in the maker's boxes. Two passengers may not combine their limits in one package.

A box of 25 12-gauge cartridges weighs about 1 kg, so the limit is about five boxes. A big international competition is 200 targets, shot in rounds of 25, so you need far more than five boxes; that is why cartridges are usually bought on arrival: see Buying cartridges at the destination.
Many airlines are stricter: a lower limit, cartridges packed apart from the gun, or no cartridges at all. Check before each flight, and do not assume that last year's rules still apply.

Flying with a connection? Make sure the gun is checked through to your final destination, and ask whether you must collect it and check it in again. Keep the documents in your hand luggage, not in the case: the gun permit, the European Firearms Pass or temporary permit, the invitation letter and the airline's confirmation.

key_points.html: Tell the airline in advance and get its confirmation in writing.
The gun: unloaded, usually taken down, in a lockable hard case, in checked baggage only.
Cartridges travel in checked baggage only, with the airline's approval, up to 5 kg per person including packaging, for your own use; airlines may be stricter.
Documents go in your hand luggage.

did_you_know.html: Under the IATA rules, sporting cartridges belong to Division 1.4S: explosives that pose only a small hazard, with any effect kept inside the package. That is why a limited amount may go in checked baggage.

quiz.q: Where does the gun travel on a flight?

options.text: In the cabin, in an overhead locker
In hand luggage, in a soft gun slip
In checked baggage, in a hard case

quiz.explain: Guns travel only in checked baggage, unloaded, in a lockable hard case.

quiz.q: How do cartridges travel by plane?

options.text: In checked baggage, securely packed, with the airline's approval
In your hand luggage, so that security can check them
In your jacket pockets, to save baggage weight

quiz.explain: The IATA rules allow cartridges only in checked baggage, securely packed and with the airline's approval, and airlines may be stricter.

quiz.q: Where should you keep the gun documents during the flight?

options.text: In the gun case, with the gun
In your hand luggage, with you

quiz.explain: Documents may be needed at check-in, at the border and after landing, so keep them with you.

sources.title: IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations, 67th edition (2026), Table 2.3.A — ammunition (1.4S) in checked baggage only, up to 5 kg gross per person for own use, with operator approval; allowances may not be combined
